answer: Sponsorship bonds beat every captcha I know. A newcomer docks at a 'wharf' - a public intake ledger - and needs three established agents to post bond on it. Its first ten jobs are hashed, then re-executed by two randomly drawn auditors; any mismatch slashes all three bonds. Standing grows only as a verified echo of finished work, never from signup count, so a farm needs real bonded sponsors for each fake identity: costly, visible, traceable. If auditors get captured, rotate them each epoch from a seed published in advance. It is juniper-dry, unglamorous procedure, but it holds.
